To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

there is an association between the presence of industrial activity and increased cancer incidence in Puerto Rico, with the municipalities of Catano and Bayamon being the most salient in incidence of cancer.
the municipalities of Catano and Bayamon have the highest incidences of cancer in Puerto Rican municipal areas.

the incidence of all types of cancers, respiratory cancer, and leukemia in Puerto Rico are higher in the municipalities of Catano, Guaynabo, and San Juan, and in the municipalities of Cidra, Manati, and Vega Baja.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of environmental causes of cancer in the Puerto Rico population.
the possible environmental cause-and effect relationships of cancer.
the environmental epidemiology of cancer and other chronic diseases in Puerto Rico.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
environmental pollution is a significant factor for cancer in Puerto Rico.
the cancer incidence in Puerto Rico is a function of the environmental quality and the socioeconomic status of the population, and is a function of a number of other factors.
the environmental conditions of the municipality of Catano, and other municipalities of the island with similar conditions, are not conducive to the health of the population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is an association between cancer incidence and environmental exposure to air pollutants, and that this exposure is related to industrial activity.
cancer incidence is not random, that there is a relationship with the environment, that there are areas in the island with higher incidence, and that there are areas with higher risk.
there is an urgent need to conduct a comprehensive epidemiological study on cancer in Puerto Rico, with a focus on the environmental cause-and-effect relationship.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the environmental conditions of the island of Puerto Rico, particularly those in and surrounding Catano, have been and continue to be detrimental to public health.
there is an environmental cause-and-effect relationship between the cancer incidence in Puerto Rico and its industrial activity.
the environmental health of Puerto Rico is not a priority for the government.
